means:
**Adjective:** biting and caustic in style — sharply, darkly critical.
**Noun (technical):** a chemical that bites into fabric so dye will fix to it.

The sting is intellectual. A cruel remark is just cruel; a **mordant** one is *clever*, dry, usually funny, and lands because it's true. The word half-praises the speaker even as it flays the target — critics, satirists and obituarists get called mordant, playground bullies never do.
trap: ⚠️ **mordant ≠ moribund.** Same *mor-* look, opposite Latin roots: *mordēre* (**to bite**) vs *morī* (**to die**). A mordant reviewer is very much alive; a moribund industry is on its way out.
trick_line: **A mordant line leaves *more dents* — teeth marks, not bruises.**
trick_unpack: Say it fast and "mordant" *is* "more dent": precise little bites of wit, not blunt-force insult.
sentences: Her memoir is **mordant** about the literary world that raised and then quietly discarded her.
He's got this **mordant** sense of humour — you laugh, then realise he just destroyed you.
in_the_wild: Still a live technical word in dyeing: alum is the classic **mordant**, the thing that bites the colour into the cloth so it won't wash out — the same bite the adjective describes.
etymology: Latin **mordēre** = *"to bite."* Same root gives **remorse** (guilt that bites you back), **morsel** (a little bite), and the musical **mordent** (a quick nipped note).
one_line: Bitingly sarcastic; sharp, dark, clever criticism.
